standard_prerequisites.name: A map of complexes K -> K tensor S over a flat ring map is a quasi-isomorphism as soon as the homology groups of K are I-power torsion and the map induces an isomorphism R/I -> S/IS on a neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces both claims to the torsion property of the homology.

standard_prerequisites.name: The homology groups of the Koszul complex K(R, f_1, ..., f_r) are I-power torsion when V(f_1, ..., f_r) = V(I)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the torsion property for the Koszul case.

standard_prerequisites.name: The homology groups of the extended alternating Cech complex on f_1, ..., f_r are I-power torsion
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the torsion property for the Cech case.

core_obligations: In both cases the source is a complex K of R-modules and the target its base change K tensor_R S, so we must show K -> K tensor_R S is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 24384-24386). By the neighbourhood-isomorphism lemma and the flatness of R -> S, this holds as soon as all homology groups of K are I-power torsion (proof lines 24386-24388). The Koszul complex has I-power torsion homology by the homotopy-koszul lemma, and the extended alternating Cech complex by the extended-alternating-torsion lemma, so both maps are quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 24388-24391).
proof_roadmap: Reformulate both claims as base change quasi-isomorphisms and reduce to I-power torsion homology (proof lines 24384-24388).
Verify the torsion property for the Koszul and Cech complexes by their lemmas (proof lines 24388-24391).
